findings.problem: This file defines two helpers, `inter_one_eq_inf` and `mem_map_of_isFibreReading`. A sibling Sol file defines both with identical statements and proofs. The same file's `solution` also proves affineness of `𝒰.inter s` for `s : 𝒰.Idx 1` with the same three-step block (`rw [inter_one_eq_inf]` then `IsSeparated.isAffineOpen_inf_and_exists_eq_sum_mul_of_isAffineOpen ... .1`). The sibling `haff` has the same text. So the same reasoning is kept in two files, and a fix to one copy will not reach the other.
findings.proposed_change: Move into one shared module, such as a small Util or Def-level file both Sol files import: (1) `inter_one_eq_inf` (verbatim); (2) `mem_map_of_isFibreReading` (verbatim; it only needs `IsFibreReading`, which is already imported); (3) a new lemma `isAffineOpen_inter_of_isSeparated {Z} {B} (f : Z ⟶ Spec B) [IsSeparated f] (𝒦 : Z.OrderedAffineCover) (s : 𝒦.Idx 1) : IsAffineOpen (𝒦.inter s)`. Its proof is `rw [inter_one_eq_inf]; exact (IsSeparated.isAffineOpen_inf_and_exists_eq_sum_mul_of_isAffineOpen f _ _ (𝒦.isAffineOpen _) (𝒦.isAffineOpen _)).1`. Both files then import it and use `haff := isAffineOpen_inter_of_isSeparated f 𝒰`. The target's `hgε` already takes `(haff s)` and calls `mem_map_of_isFibreReading ... (hread s)`, so it is unchanged. The sibling's `heq` uses `(haff s)` and `h3 s`, so it is unchanged too. Both files keep their current imports plus the new module. No hypotheses change, because the statements are copied unchanged.
findings.benefit: There is one definition of each fact, so a signature change or instance-set change is made once. Each `solution` also gets shorter.
